_about: Build N (mockup R56): the cloud AI companies, read by cloud_ai.py and by the page. Every fact and link was read on the live pages on 19 Oct 2026. Numbers change often, so the page shows none: it links to each company's own limits page. NeuroVault ships no key: each person adds their own (Windows Credential Manager).
sent: Your question and the note or notes it’s about (this note, or your newest notes), or the text of another AI job you send there.

providers.name: Groq
providers.keep: Groq says it doesn’t keep what you send, except logs it may keep for up to 30 days to fix faults or look into abuse. Its data page doesn’t say whether it trains on it.
providers.steps: Sign in with Google or an email, open API Keys, press Create API key and copy it.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.short: May use it, with human review
providers.keep: On the free tier, Google may use it, with human review, to improve its products, and asks you not to send anything private. In the UK, the EEA and Switzerland it doesn’t, as on the paid tier.
providers.steps: Sign in with a Google account, press Create API key and copy it.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.who: OpenRouter, Inc., in the USA. It passes your text to the company that runs the model
providers.keep: OpenRouter keeps it only if you opt in, but some free models are run by companies that may keep it or train on it. You can turn those off in your OpenRouter privacy settings.
providers.steps: Sign in, open Keys, press Create Key and copy it.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.keep: Cloudflare says it doesn’t train AI models on it and doesn’t keep it once it has answered.
providers.steps: Sign in, copy your Account ID from the dashboard, then make an API token that can use Workers AI.

providers.name: Cerebras
providers.keep: Cerebras says it doesn’t keep what you send or what it answers. Its free start is trial credit that runs out, not a free plan.
providers.steps: Sign in, open API Keys and copy your key.

providers.name: Hugging Face
providers.who: Hugging Face, Inc., in the USA. It passes your text to the partner that runs the model
providers.keep: Hugging Face says it doesn’t store what you send or what comes back (it keeps logs for up to 30 days). The partner that runs the model has its own terms. A free account has no credit for this: it needs Hugging Face PRO or prepaid credit.
providers.steps: Sign in, open Access Tokens, make a token that can “Make calls to Inference Providers” and copy it.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.keep: Anthropic’s commercial terms say it may not train its models on what you send through its API.
providers.steps: Sign in, add a payment card, open API keys, press Create Key and copy it.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.keep: OpenAI says it doesn’t train on what you send through its API unless you opt in. It may keep it for up to 30 days to check for abuse.
providers.steps: Sign in, add a payment card, open API keys, press Create new secret key and copy it.

_reasoning: QC 94 (19 Oct 2026, read on each company's reasoning docs): params are sent as they are; tokens is the length field it takes; min_tokens is the least length a thinking model gets (its thinking counts toward it); temperature false = not sent (Anthropic refuses one below 1; OpenAI's reasoning models take none).
_models: QC 91: models_url lists the company's models (only the key is sent); the list is kept in LOCALAPPDATA/NeuroVault/cloud_models.json and the fixed model is the fallback.
